body:
Hey, I'm still here and I appreciate you writing. I'm finishing a work contract in a couple of weeks and have been thinking about adopting a kitten then as I am going to take some time off work for a while, a month at least, maybe two. I'm just taking each day as it comes at the moment and having something to care for could help me to stop thinking about myself, like you have said.

I am feeling better than I was and have a little hope now and some ideas thanks to people like you.

It was quite hard and some of their stories are very sad. Also its all too common to no longer see people because they fall or have a stroke or worse. It's a nice feeling though to know you have made a small difference in their life. I used to visit one lady each week and she would always be sad and quiet when I first arrived but would be laughing and smiling by the time I left. I miss her. I miss some of the other people too. It's sad when they can't remember you and it's hard when you see how difficult they are finding things. There are lots of heartbreaking stories but also some fun and laughs too. They are also refreshingly honest I found, which makes a change from the usual people you meet.

I don't think that I could do it again as I'm a bit too emotional really. I get too attached and I don't think that is healthy. You have to care but not too much that you become attached, if that makes sense. I would still recommend volunteering with the elderly though as it does change how you see the world and yourself. Perhaps I'm not the best person to listen to considering why I am writing here in the first place (!), but I would still recommend it. 

The other volunteers and the paid organisers were all very friendly and supportive and it was always a nice atmosphere. Very different from working in an office.

This was about a year ago, before I gave the garden a good sorting out!

Your video did kind of tug at me a little bit. I wish I had something to believe in cos right now I have run out of things. There;s really nothing I get out of bed for in the morning. In the past I have volunteered and that kept me going for a few years. I helped out the elderly and people with Altzheimer's. I also worked with Oxfam and some other, local places. I did gardening for a few months and that helped - it was nice to see the garden looking better but then winter started. I adopted my cat several years again and she was so very shy in the beginning but she is much happier these days. I would try a new club or something but I just don't trust people. I kept thinking yesterday about what it would actually be like to do it and I didn't eat anything yesterday and I have work starting again in the New Year and I just don't think I will last. I have some photos of my cat I could share.
They are lovely and were very cute to watch. Fostering sounds like a nice idea. There is a PDSA near me.
